title: Application of Mobile Phone Location Data in Earthquake Emergency Work
author: Xia Chaoxu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wq4fdyw

steps.title: Collect Mobile Phone Location Data
steps.instruction: Acquire phone location data from Jiuzhaigou County for two specific time periods to establish a baseline and observe earthquake impact.

substeps.instruction: Collect data from 2 hours before the earthquake to 8 hours after (19:00 on August 8th to 5:00 on August 9th), totaling 10 hours of data.
Collect data for the same time period on the day before the earthquake for comparison.

steps.title: Process and Analyze Signal Trends
steps.instruction: Process the obtained mobile phone signals using a grid-based approach to analyze temporal trends.

substeps.instruction: Perform grid-processing on the number of mobile phone signals.
Integrate and statistically analyze the data within the grids.
Determine change trends for the study area across three periods: before the earthquake, during the earthquake hit, and after the earthquake.

steps.title: Calculate Data Change Rates
steps.instruction: Analyze the data change rates at specific time intervals relative to the earthquake event.

substeps.instruction: Select data change rates for 21:09 (10 minutes before), 21:19 (earthquake time), and 21:29 (10 minutes after).
Calculate the change rate where Na is the signal number of the previous stage and Nb is the signal number of the later stage.
Identify instances where α is 0, indicating the signal number of the latter phase is greater than the previous phase.

steps.title: Categorize Signal Data Overlap
steps.instruction: Classify the processed data into overlapping and non-overlapping categories to determine personnel movement.

substeps.instruction: Identify overlapping data: where the number of signals before the earthquake equals the number at the time of the earthquake, indicating no change or movement of personnel.
Identify non-overlapping data: where data or locations differ before and after the earthquake (e.g., data exists before but not after, or vice versa).

steps.title: Analyze Buffer Zone Change Rates
steps.instruction: Evaluate the change rate of signal data based on the distance from the epicenter.

substeps.instruction: Establish buffer zones at distances of 15km, 20km, 40km, and 80km from the epicenter.
Analyze the change rate of signal data within these different buffer zones relative to time and distance.
